newsitem.title: JAPAN: TOCOM precious metals slip on yen's rebound.
newsitem.headline: TOCOM precious metals slip on yen's rebound.

text.p: Yen-based Tokyo precious metals futures extended early losses to end lower across the board on Tuesday, in line with the yen's moderate rebound against the dollar late in the day, traders said.
Gold futures ranged from two yen to eight yen per gram lower. Benchmark February was off eight yen at 1,392 yen.
Traders were tending to hold a moderately bearish view of gold futures, amid expectations that spot gold prices had more scope to decline and that the dollar's rise against the yen had now stalled.
In the bullion market, spot gold was quoted easier at $345.40/70 per ounce at the Tokyo close, against $346.00/50 in New York on Monday.

Sporadic selling by Japanese trade houses dented spot gold, while private investors stayed mostly on the sidelines in the gold futures market, holding little hope that prices would rise significantly at this stage, traders said.

In platinum futures, two-way trade was detected earlier in the day but the market later followed spot prices lower. Palladium futures also extended early losses on sporadic selling pressure from private investors.
Traders said the recent slip in palladium futures suggested that market players were expecting Russian sales in the spot market in the near future.

"Russia may be under pressure to resume sales in the spot market, but uncertainty remains over the availability of Russian metal for export," one trader said. Given persistently high short-term lease rates around 10 percent, he said volatile trading in palladium would continue.
Benchmark February platinum was off 14 yen per gram at 1,461 yen. Benchmark palladium was off 11 yen per gram at 595 yen.
Benchmark silver was off 0.7 yen per 10 grams at 193.0 yen.
